title: Scholar's mate and how to stop it
line: Queen and bishop on f7 in four moves, and the moves that make it harmless.

steps.text: After 1.e4 e5, the weakest square in Black's camp is f7. Only the king guards it.
Put the bishop where it aims at f7.

wrong.d1h5: The queen aims at f7 too, but out this early she is easy to chase. Bring the bishop out first.

steps.hint: The bishop on f1 can reach a square on the same diagonal as f7.
steps.after: The bishop on c4 looks straight at f7.

steps.text: Bring the queen to h5. Then the queen and the bishop both aim at f7.

wrong.d1f3: Qf3 aims at f7 too. In this lesson, take her to h5.

steps.hint: The queen goes to the edge of the board, on the h-file.
steps.after: Two pieces aim at f7, and one defends it.

steps.text: Black attacks the queen with the knight and forgets about f7. Finish the game.

wrong.h5e5: That is check, but the knight on c6 takes the queen.
wrong.c4f7: That is check, but the king steps to e7. Take on f7 with the queen instead.

steps.hint: Take on f7 with the piece the bishop guards.
steps.after: Checkmate. The bishop guards the queen, and the king has no square.

steps.text: Now play Black, after Qh5. Stop the mate on f7 with a pawn move that also attacks the queen.

also.d8e7: That guards f7 too. This lesson goes on with g6.

steps.hint: A pawn next to the king can step forward and attack h5.
steps.after: The queen is attacked and has to move.

steps.text: The queen comes back to f3 and aims at f7 again. Block her line with a knight.
steps.hint: The knight on g8 can step into the queen's path.
steps.after: f7 is safe, and a knight is out.

summary: The queen and bishop can mate on f7 in four moves. g6 and Nf6 stop it.
